The 2027 Frank Lloyd Wright Airstream Holds Its Own as the Most Beautiful Travel Trailer Around
17 photos
Photo: Airstream
There's always room for improvement, as the saying goes. That's true, but not where it concerns "the perfect" Airstream, because obviously, perfection can't be improved. Case in point: the limited edition Frank Lloyd Wright Airstream, now at the 2027 model year.
Airstream announced the Frank Lloyd Wright Limited Edition in the summer of 2025, for what was then the 2026 model year. They said from the start that this series would be limited to just 200 units, parsed out over several years, which bring us to today.
This special edition Airstream is now at the 2027 model year and it's yet to reach the 100th unit. This being such a rare and absolutely beautiful Airstream , taking it in visually is better than nothing at all, so take a few minutes to revisit it with me. Below is the 81st unit built, presented with the purpose of securing a buyer.
The 2027 Frank Lloyd Wright Airstream is more of the same, which is a delicate way of saying that nothing has changed about it from the debut year. Actually, strike that: something did change – not with the trailer itself but pricing, which now starts higher than it did last year.
Photo: Airstream Still, this is, without a doubt, the most beautiful Airstream ever created, and quite possibly one of the most beautiful travel trailers around.
Frank Lloyd Wright is one of the best known and internationally appreciated American architects and designer. His particular style, called organic architecture, embraced core principles like harmony with nature, total, cohesive design where every bit was considered an integral part of the architectural piece, the concept of compression and release, and the so-called "destruction of the box," where isolated rooms were replaced by spaces that flowed one into the other.
All these are apparent in the Frank Lloyd Wright-badged Airstream , which was designed in collaboration with the Lloyd Wright Foundation. Also called the Frank Lloyd Wright Usonian Limited Edition 28RB, it's built on the same body as the International 28RB or the Globetrotter 27FB, but with a fully custom floorplan that makes it the only Airstream with a king bedroom.
Photo: Airstream Inc. This Airstream sits on a boxed steel frame and features the iconic "silver bullet" aluminum body over an aluminum ribbed frame, with composite flooring, full insulation throughout, and the Airstream windows, including the staple Vista View clerestory-style windows, with tinted glass, integrated bug screens, and hand-rived aluminum frames.
Riding on twin axles with Dexter spring suspension and self-adjusting brakes, the Airstream gets power stabilizer jacks, manual awnings on three sides, and rock stone guards on both the body and the front windows. Overall length is 28 feet 2 inches (8.5 meters), and you get 6.7 feet (2 meters) of headroom inside, and 8 feet (2.4 meters) in width, so there's enough space to actually build an architectural, home-like, gorgeous space.
The chassis being similar to that on an International 28RB, you get a tailgate entry that allows you to open up the rear of the trailer to the elements – and whatever view you happen to be parked by. The main bedroom is at the back, but you wouldn't be able to tell it in day mode, as you get a pair of face-to-face comfy sofas that turn this into the second lounge available onboard.
Photo: Airstream Inc. The first one is at the entrance: a beautiful couch wrapping around the front end and turning into a double bed only when needed. In Frank Lloyd Wright style, this Airstream combines materials and fabrics and colors in unexpected ways, to incredible results.
The geometric pattern on the inside of the entry door and laser-cut into the screen door is also found in the dining table, on the kitchen backsplash, and on light fixtures. You have aluminum walls, as you'd expect in an Airstream, but also custom cabinetry of real wood, composite surfaces, and luscious, light fabrics, all of them made to look their best with indirect lighting.
Storage is limited to the lower part of the trailer , with the exception of the narrow hallway that connects the two living areas, where you have floor to ceiling storage across the bathroom. This Special Edition also strives to hide everything you don't want to see from sight, so the TV and sound system, the fridge, and even the dining table are masked from sight by natural wood.
Photo: Airstream Inc. The galley is on the campside, with a three-burner gas cooktop and a massive stainless steel sink set into a composite countertop with beautiful wood finish. Below, you get a convection microwave with an air fryer function and plenty of storage for the basics.
Across the way is an extended counter that hides an extendable dining table and a fold-up workstation. Also built into it is storage for two expandable wooden chairs, so in between the couch, a small footstool, and these two chairs, you can host a nice dinner or gaming party.
The TV and Bluetooth stereo sound is behind a hinged wooden door on the wall. Airstream uses the same kind of door, only of a much bigger size, for the wardrobe, thus coming up with a very discreet solution to a practical, everyday feature.
Photo: Airstream Inc. The bathroom is behind a black panel wall with wooden slats and a smoked porthole with the same geometrical motif. It's a full, three-piece bathroom with a macerator-style porcelain toilet, a stainless steel sink with integrated storage, and a walk-in shower with a seat.
Nice details, like a sliding medicine cabinet door that reveals access to the porthole window, and another matching light fixture, add extra style to a space you wouldn't normally think of in terms of "stylish."
The rear lounge offers sleeping in separate twin beds or in a full king, as the couches join in the middle at the press of a button. Airstream builds storage under each for the essentials, adding an extra-wide open shelf at the back for more items you will want handy.
Photo: Airstream Inc. This Airstream comes started with a 15,000-BTU Coleman-Mach AC in the back and a 13,500-BTU unit in the front, both ducted and with heat pumps, a 30,000-BTU furnace that also heats the holding tanks, a MaxxAir power fan with a rain sensor, an Aqua-hot tankless water heater, a full-size spare on an undermounted carrier, and a solar system with 300W of solar on the roof, a 2000W inverter, and a pair of 500kWh batteries.
In terms of holding tanks, you get 37 gallons (140 liters) for freshwater, 40 gallons (151 liters) for gray, and 35 gallons (132 liters) for black water.
The Frank Lloyd Wright Airstream comes in at 6,900 lbs (3,130 kg) dry and has a gross vehicle weight of 7,600 lbs (3,447 kg), so you have about 700 lbs (317 kg) of cargo carrying capacity.
Photo: Airstream Inc. Starting price has gone up since the last time we looked at this special edition and now sits at $189,900. It's true that each unit is a complete solution, ready to hit the road from the moment of delivery, but you can still add other Frank Lloyd Wright-branded items like cutting boards, exterior graphics, and a teak shower mat, and all these will add to the final sale price.

source_document.body:
The Pacific Maritime Association and International Longshore and Warehouse Union Local 26 have reached a tentative contract agreement covering about 250 watchmen at the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach, averting an immediate strike threat at the busiest U.S. trade gateway.
The agreement, under federal mediation, remains subject to ratification by Local 26 members. The existing contract will be extended while that process proceeds, the PMA said.
In its announcement, the employers’ association thanked the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service, the U.S. Department of Labor and Local 26’s bargaining committee for their work. It said the agreement would provide greater certainty for the ports, cargo owners, supply-chain workers and the regional and national economies.
No terms or timeline for ratification were disclosed.
The tentative settlement follows more than a year of bargaining. The previous contract expired in July 2025, and subsequent extensions allowed negotiations to continue. The latest deadline had been set for 12:01 a.m. Nov. 21, raising the prospect of a walkout if the parties failed to reach a deal or agree to another extension.
Union members had authorized a strike in late October. Federally mediated negotiations resumed Friday after an earlier bargaining session ended without a breakthrough.
Before the settlement, PMA said its offer included a $3,200 one-time bonus and wage increases that would lift average annual earnings for full-time watchmen from more than $170,000 to $198,000. The employers’ proposal also included continued fully employer-paid healthcare for active workers and retirees and higher pension benefits.
FreightWaves has reached out to Local 26 for comment.
Local 26’s watchmen provide security at six container terminals across the two ports. Their duties include controlling terminal-gate access, conducting security patrols and reporting safety issues.
There were concerns that cargo operations would be disrupted if other union workers honored watchmen picket lines.
PMA has said Local 26 represents roughly 2% of ILWU workers at the two ports.
Why it matters: The agreement reduces the immediate risk of a labor disruption at the nation’s busiest container port complex, where interruptions could affect cargo owners and businesses throughout the supply chain.

2027 Hyundai Elantra & 2028 Elantra Hybrid: How Do They Compare to Other Affordable Compact Sedans?
11 photos
Photo: Hyundai
The eighth generation of the ubiquitous compact and affordable sedan has arrived in front of the global audience at the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show . And no, you’re not having déjà vu, as the model has already been shown before as the KDM-specification Hyundai Avante back in June during the Busan International Mobility Show at home in South Korea.
Now, the compact sedan series with many names – it’s known as the Hyundai Elantra globally and in North America specifically, but also as the i30 Sedan in Australia, besides Avante at home in South Korea- introduces the bold Art of Steel design alongside the all-new Tucson. It also packs advanced connectivity and safety technology, as well as expanded passenger space because it’s larger.
Hyundai Motor America unveiled the all-new 2027 Elantra and 2028 Elantra Hybrid at AutoMobility LA 2026 at the Los Angeles Auto Show, introducing the latest iteration of one of the brand’s most successful and longest-running nameplates – the first generation launched in 1990, almost three decades ago.
Since passenger cars are currently in jeopardy due to the continued success of crossovers, SUVs, and trucks, Hyundai wanted to expand Elantra’s appeal “beyond traditional compact sedan expectations, (so) this all-new model pairs a bold and muscular look, closer to midsize-class passenger space, the Pleos Connect infotainment, and enhanced safety features.”
Photo: Hyundai It’s also available with both ICE and hybrid powertrains , with the longer wheelbase designed to provide “generous interior room approaching mid-size dimensions and best-in-class rear passenger space,” including 39.1 inches of rear legroom, and Pleos Connect, Hyundai’s new Android Automotive OS-based infotainment and connectivity hub, packs a 12.9-inch Full HD display and the Gleo AI voice assistant plus over-the-air update features.
Hyundai makes a statement with the design of the Elantra and Tucson , again reshuffling expectations, and the Elantra looks like an N model without actually paying the premium, if you ask us. That’s not a bad idea, since the competition may be dwindling, but it remains absolutely laser-focused, including in the United States.
What remains to be seen is whether Hyundai is going in the right direction with the design that is deeply connected between the Elantra and Tucson and probably upcoming new models, while the interior is now mostly the same, featuring the big central screen, the same dashboard layout, and a slim 9.9-inch digital instrument cluster display atop the dashboard, seen by the driver above, not through the steering wheel.
Photo: Hyundai Under the hood, though, Hyundai plays it safe – and according to the current preferences of customers. In the United States, Hyundai will introduce the 2027 Elantra ICE with the SE, SEL Sport, and Limited trim levels rocking the same 2.0-liter four-pot with front-wheel drive and 147 hp, along with a combined rating of up to 35 MPG.
All models are now 3.4 inches longer, 1.2 inches wider, and 0.4 inches taller for the ICE model, and feature a wheelbase that has grown by 1.2 inches compared to the outgoing model. As for the 2028 Hyundai Elantra Hybrid, which obviously has late 2027 availability, the grades include SE Blue, SEL Sport Hybrid, and Limited Hybrid trims with an electrified 1.6-liter engine packing a combined 155 hp and up to 53 MPG combined.
Importantly, the Elantra Hybrid will arrive with a better rear suspension – a multi-link independent setup versus ICE’s coupled torsion beam. Alas, that doesn’t mean that either will have an easy time across the US compact sedan segment when they arrive at dealerships.
Photo: Hyundai The competition is pretty stiff and offers quite a lot of options, actually. We start randomly with the Honda Civic, which just got updated for the 2027 model year with increased pricing (+$300 across the board) and a new Sport-L grade. The prices are not important at the moment since we don’t know the MSRPs from Hyundai, but the 2027 Honda Civic offers plenty of punch – the Sedan body style has a 2.0-liter with 150 hp for the ICE model, while the Civic Hybrid easily bests the Elantra Hybrid with its two-motor system with a combined 200 hp.
Next up comes the ubiquitous Toyota Corolla, which is well known for its iconic reliability and great hybrid powertrain – though it’s obviously way blander than the new Elantra, just like the Civic. Options include the regular Corolla 2.0L with 169 hp, while the hybrid model is less potent at 138 combined hp. We’re not done yet, by the way.
The Kia cousin has the new K4 on offer, which replaced the Forte with an equally bold design like the Elantra, plus the same base engine with 147 hp. Kia also boasts a more potent 1.6-liter turbo with 190 hp if you can’t wait for the Elantra N, but in turn doesn’t offer a hybrid option. The Nissan Sentra has been completely redesigned for the 2026 model year and packs a 2.0-liter with 149 hp and the Xtronic CVT, but again lacks a hybrid option.
Miscellaneous options also include the Mazda3, which is way sportier with a 2.5-liter in NA or turbo form with 186 or 250 hp, as well as the Volkswagen Jetta, a classic compact German sedan packing standard turbo powertrains for added sportiness – the 1.5-liter has 158 hp and the 2.0-liter rocks 228 ponies in GLI specification. The Perfect Coastal Tiny House Exists, and It Comes from Tasmania
30 photos
Photo: Artisan Tiny Homes
For us folks in the Northern Hemisphere, winter is fast approaching, bringing thoughts of snow, chilly mornings, and outdoor fun in the mountains, but this perfect beach tiny house from Tasmania has the power to transport us straight into the ultimate summer vacation near the ocean.
Who better than Australians to create and build the best beach tiny homes? Experts in the coastal lifestyle where every single day feels like an amazing vacation, people in Australia have also learned to develop the kind of homes on wheels that can withstand the specific challenges of the country’s climate and environment.
Little Whaler was born in Tasmania, which makes its carefree, adventurous, and natural spirit even stronger. Custom-crafted to be enjoyed during beach holidays, this stylish tiny house is a perfect refuge for fishing enthusiasts, ocean lovers, and anyone looking to life the coastal lifestyle to the fullest. Everything about the Little Whaler screams “coastal”, from the aesthetic itself to the straightforward functionality and laid-back comfort.
A beautiful color palette with bold accents of bright blue highlights an interior covered in shadow plywood paneling. Huge windows, many of them with awning opening, blur the line between the inside and the outside, bringing that wonderful ocean breeze in. An efficient layout, specifically requested by the owners, ensures comfortable accommodation for the main residents on the ground floor, and for guests in the loft area.
Photo: Artisan Tiny Homes Perhaps the only thing that differentiates Little Whaler from traditional beach tiny houses is the size. With its nine-meter (29.5 feet) length and 4.3-meter (14 feet) height, this spacious mobile home can easily sleep up to four people without sacrificing any of the standard living spaces. In fact, these dimensions and the flexible two-bedroom configuration would seem to indicate a well-suited full-time residence.
However, Little Whaler’s owners envisioned it as a welcoming, spacious vacation home, specifically for beach holidays near the ocean. From the outside, the strong asymmetrical profile, described by the builder as “wedge-shaped” indicates the presence of one loft, added to a ground floor with generous floor space.
The multitude of windows, plus an extra-wide, fully-glazed entrance, make this tiny home typically Aussie.
Far from any conventional minimalism and with no hint of Scandian style whatsoever, this Tasmanian gem is fully of personality, expressed including via the bold colors and textures. On the outside, the asymmetrical silhouette is highlighted even more by the beautiful texture of the natural Cypress cladding, partnered with metal accents in a “Deep Ocean” shade, and black window frames throughout.
Against the striking Cypress cladding with the aged look of an old beach house, the plywood interior looks even warmer, softer, and cozier, and it’s this powerful contrast that makes Little Whaler’s style so unique. The white VJ lining boards on the ceiling add a contemporary touch, keeping the overall style clean, yet not minimalist in a basic sense. Deep blue accents throughout, from doors to cabinets and textiles, bring the whole interior to life.
Photo: Artisan Tiny Homes The owners specifically requested a downstairs bedroom for themselves, as well as a comfortable loft for their guests. Style-wise, they preferred to keep things functional, but with a dash a luxury sprinkled throughout.
This brief was a perfect task for the Artisan Tiny Homes team – as the name of this Tasmania-based builder suggests, they are experts in creating outstanding, bespoke homes on wheels. In almost a decade of operations, they have delivered less than 40 homes, precisely because each one was like a finely polished, exquisite jewel of unique beauty.
The family behind this impressive brand is like the dream team of tiny houses, comprised of Kerrie, who brings her incredibly talented and sophisticated touch as an artist and interior designer, her husband Kevin, who is not only a builder but also a restorer, and their daughter, who has followed in their footsteps as a carpenter.
All Artisan Tiny Homes are simply gorgeous, inside-out, and the Little Whaler is no exception. The subtle take on a classic nautical theme, combined with the pampering comfort of a spacious layout, makes this one of the best beach tiny homes. The builder has also ingeniously created a pop-out that expands the living room area. That allows for an open lounge that feels more like a cozy nook, in addition to the spacious ground-floor bedroom, kitchen, and bathroom.
Photo: Artisan Tiny Homes Accommodation inside the Little Whaler exudes the exact kind of effortless comfort and peaceful styling you’d expect in a vacation tiny house on the beach. The main bedroom fits a queen-sized bed, and it comes with a huge built-in, open-shelf wardrobe, and multiple large windows that recreate the effect of an oversized panoramic window. That is why the room feels even bigger than its actual size, and extra-bright.
The downstairs placement makes it easily accessible for anyone (who doesn’t love a tiny house ground-floor bedroom?), while also allowing the owners to adjust the level of privacy to their liking. The loft bedroom is accessed via a plain ladder, precisely because it’s only meant for temporary guest accommodation. However, the room itself is spacious, with abundant walk-around space for the two-person bed, and generous windows for a light-filled ambiance.
For a tiny weekender on wheels, Little Whaler boasts an impressive kitchen. An L-shaped countertop offers excellent space for preparing meals, and also incorporates a proper lineup of lower cupboards. A couple of upper cupboards were also added to the wall near the bathroom door, taking advantage of every inch of available space, but still making room for big awning windows – a must-have in every Aussie tiny house kitchen.
The full-size pantry right behind the loft ladder is one of the highlights of this modern, bright kitchen. There’s also dedicated space for a fridge, and even a dishwasher. Again, considering that the ground floor also houses a spacious, enclosed bedroom, and a lovely lounge, this is a remarkably big and well-appointed kitchen, which confirms how practical this tiny house layout is overall.
Photo: Artisan Tiny Homes Behind a bright blue door that doubles as a decorative accent, Little Whaler hides a compact, but fully-equipped bathroom with a clean aesthetic. The fully-tiled shower with a double window and a custom screen adds a touch of luxury, while the custom-crafted vanity under the sink provides essential storage. All the appliances are conventional, since this mobile house was meant to be connected to standard utilities.
Waterproof flooring throughout adds to this tiny home’s resilience, especially in a more humid climate, also ensuring low-maintenance over time. The flexible layout and timeless coastal aesthetic mean that this tiny house can easily switch from beachy weekender to full-time residences, which allows more options for the owners in the future.
There’s something about Australian craftsmanship in general that makes tiny homes feel completely effortless, even when they are built and styled with extreme attention to detail. It’s the same carefree vibe that defines an Aussie beachside vacation so well, and that so many people all over the world crave for.
Photo: Artisan Tiny Homes The Little Whaler embodies both the spirit and the aesthetic of a Tasmanian beach tiny house, and it makes it look so easy. If coastal tiny homes ever seemed too small or too plaint, this tiny gem on wheels is here to give you everything that was missing from the ones before – luscious comfort, smart functionality, and the spacious accommodation of a bigger house.

Elroy Air Scores a $70M Deal for Its Autonomous Heavy-Cargo Drone in the UAE
10 photos
Photo: Elroy Air
Elroy Air, the name behind one of the most innovative and advanced autonomous, hybrid-electric cargo VTOLs (vertical takeoff and landing) in the US, is taking new steps to increase its presence in the UAE, one of the biggest and most promising markets for AAM (Advanced Air Mobility) overall.
US-based technology company Elroy Air is gearing up to end the year on a high note, with one of its most significant purchase deals so far. This new agreement with the Abu Dhabi-based Barq Group is big not just because of the actual monetary value (a total of $70 million, starting with a $10.25 million initial deposit), but also because it opens the door to an extended presence in the MENA space (Middle East and North Africa) market.
In fact, this purchase agreement between Elroy Air and Barq Group is only a part of a much more ambitious, large-scale plan. The two have previously confirmed plans for a joint venture that will support a manufacturing and service facility in Abu Dhabi, specifically dedicated to producing and distributing the Chaparral cargo drone in the entire MENA region, which would translate to a huge step up for Elroy Air.
In the meantime, the Chaparral VTOL drones agreed upon through this recent collaboration will be manufactured in the US. More specifically, Elroy’s exclusive US manufacturer, Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, will start rolling out these drones at its facility in Sacramento, California. Production is set to begin here before the end of this year, with first deliveries to Barq Group in Abu Dhabi scheduled for the beginning of next year.
The contract specifies five firm orders plus 15 production slot reservations, with the condition that Barq Group will make pre-delivery payments for all the reservations. According to Elroy, the initial deposit will help fund half of the price of each of the five Chaparral drones included in the firm order.
The Chaparral VTOL drone brings together multiple advantages, from the hybrid-electric propulsion and vertical landing ability to a fully automated cargo loading/unloading process. The pod at the center of its unique cargo system needs to be only pre-loaded by personnel, after which the VTOL picks it up, delivers, and unloads it at the destination without any human intervention.
The vertical takeoff and landing capability allows the Chaparral to operate independently of any conventional runways or airstrips, and its electric propulsion supported by a hybrid system is also not dependent on dedicated charging infrastructure. An extended range of over 300 miles (483 km) is coupled with a heavy-payload cargo of up to 300 lbs (136 kg).
Chaparral is the only autonomous, hybrid-electric heavy-cargo drone that was selected to participate in the eIPP , America’s pioneering electric aviation and AAM initiative.

Opel's New Leapmotor-Developed Compact SUV Expected to Start Production in September 2028
20 photos
Photo: Opel
Back in the day, Opel used to be GM's most popular European subsidiary. The Detroit-based automaker controlled the German automaker through 2017, when French colossus Groupe PSA acquired both Opel and Vauxhall from General Motors. Both marques became subsidiaries of Stellantis in 2021, further diluting their characters. Oh, and it's about to get weirder in 2028!
Per a media release from Opel, its chief executive officer and the big kahuna at Leapmotor Global have signed a deal according to which the Chinese brand will help Opel develop a new compact SUV . Before going any further, Leapmotor is known as Zhejiang Leapmotor Technology Co., Ltd., and this entity controls 49 percent of the international division that runs all overseas businesses.
Stellantis is listed with 51 percent, and Leapmotor Global is the consumer-facing branding of Leapmotor International. Pretty straightforward thus far, right? As part of the Opel-Leapmotor agreement, said compact SUV will use components from Leapmotor, styling and chassis engineering from Opel, and so forth. Production will be handled by the Stellantis Zaragoza plant in Spain.
The cited media release reveals that sales are expected to start in 2028, yet a Zhejiang Leapmotor Technology filing with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange reveals that Leapmotor is committing 100 million euros under the cooperation agreement, which is a relatively small amount of money when you think about it.
Engineering and development work is scheduled to kick off by the end of the year, continue into 2027, and part of 2028 to boot. The anticipated SOP date is September 2028, meaning that Opel's Chinese crossover would hit dealers as a 2029 model. In the first half of 2028, production readiness will be the focus.
Photo: Leapmotor The contractual arrangement further stipulates that Opel retains full responsibility for the overall product cost target, while Leapmotor has to make commercially reasonable efforts to support that objective. You can easily interpret this as making sure the newcomer remains commercially viable, but if you ask me, that's cost-cutting lingo right there.
Opel will also conduct durability, static, and dynamic evaluations, and the evaluation results are to be discussed with Leapmotor. Regarding the Chinese partner, supporting Opel in achieving the crossover's overall total product cost target by supplying core components also sounds like a very cost-sensitive program.
If you have ever driven a Stellantis-era Opel or Vauxhall, you already know their material quality and reliability leave much to be desired. Instead of bashing the new collab, I'd wager that a Leapmotor-flavored Opel has the makings of a better overall package than a Stellantis-only product.
My biggest concern here is that Opel risks losing its role as a bona fide developer to become an integrator. The agreement paints a reasonable division of labor until you consider the finest of details. While there is nothing wrong with outsourcing parts, will Opel retain sufficient engineering authority to make the finished product recognizably Opel?
The collab's terms also indicate that Leapmotor has more to gain from a strategic standpoint, with said collaboration providing the Chinese party firsthand insight into European customers' preferences, more experience with European vehicle development requirements, and improvements in engineering know-how. And lest we forget, Stellantis is already building a Leapmotor model at the group's Zaragoza plant in Spain.
Said model is the B10 crossover, namely a compact that may very well become the half-brother of the yet-unnamed Opel crossover. Under this production arrangement, Leapmotor found a way to avoid China-origin vehicle duties while also lowering logistics costs. On that note, where would the new sport utility vehicle fit into Opel's current sport utility vehicle range?
Following the canning of the Crossland, the German marque currently has the B-segment Mokka, the B-/C-segment Frontera, and the C-segment Grandland. Another compact sounds like an overlap, but as you already know, compact means many things nowadays. Due to Leapmotor's engineering, we can imagine a lower-cost model slotting between the Frontera and Grandland in the crossover range.

Israeli AIR Autonomous Cargo Aircraft Set to Start Flight Tests in Florida
8 photos
Photo: AIR VEV
AIR VEV, the Israel-based maker of the famous Air One personal eVTOL (electric vertical takeoff and landing), has officially sent its first Air 120D cargo aircraft to its Florida headquarters, for flight demonstrations. This autonomous cargo version of the popular Air One shows promising potential for the US Air Force and beyond.
AIR VEV is particularly known for Air One, the exciting two-seat personal aircraft currently working to secure the FAA (Federal Aviation Administration) Light Sport Aircraft certification, but the Israeli company also makes an autonomous cargo version, the Air 120D, with excellent capabilities for defense and contested logistics, in addition to commercial cargo and humanitarian missions.
A few months ago, AIR had officially announced a major partnership with FDOT (Florida Department of Transportation) that would allow it to start manufacturing its eVTOLs in the US. FDOT named AIR as the first company that will produce and operate eVTOLs in Florida under the SunTrax umbrella, one of the most important and ambitious AAM (Advanced Air Mobility) initiatives in the US so far.
SunTrax is meant to operate as a special campus for testing both air and ground advanced mobility solutions, via the SunTrax Ground and SunTrax Air divisions. As a result, AIR has established its new US headquarters here, at the Orlando-based SunTrax hub, confirming plans to kick off flight plans for both the Air One and Air 120D here.
The arrival of the first Air 120D aircraft marks the first step in this large-scale plan aiming for commercial production in the near future. According to the Israeli company, its autonomous cargo aircraft falls under the US Department of War Group 4 UAS category, which makes it compatible with defense logistics in contested environments and environments with little to no infrastructure.
As a completely autonomous aircraft, the Air 120D eliminates risks for human personnel, while accessing remote areas thanks to its vertical takeoff and landing capabilities that don’t require conventional airstrips or infrastructure. These capabilities also make it compatible with maritime logistics and humanitarian aid. In terms of cargo capacity, the Air 120 D is designed to carry around 550 pounds in a 70-cubic-foot cargo bay.
This past summer, AIR has also officially unveiled the popular Air One personal eVTOL at the 2026 EEA AirVenture event in Oshkosh. The Israeli company was actively involved in developing the MOSAIC regulatory framework alongside FAA, ASTM (American Society for Testing and Materials), and civil aviation authorities from other countries.
This new legislation is said to bridge the gap between light-category aircraft (the existing regulatory framework for aircraft like the Air One), and new-generation eVTOL aircraft.

Electric vehicles have finally gone mainstream in Grand Theft Auto. In GTA 6, EVs are just part of everyday traffic in Vice City, from Tesla and Porsche lookalikes to a parody of Electrify America’s charging network.
It’s a big change for a series that spent over a decade treating EVs as a Tesla joke. After a few days of playing, I’d say Rockstar nailed the vibe.
I’ve been playing GTA 6 since it launched on Thursday, partly for fun and partly because I wanted to see how Rockstar would handle EVs this time. The answer: a lot better than I expected.
From the Keys to Vice City
The game starts you in the Keys, Rockstar’s take on the Florida Keys, and it’s a rougher part of Leonida. Lots of older cars and beaters, and you won’t see many EVs.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
That changes as you head north to Vice City, the game’s version of Miami. The closer you get, the more electric cars show up in traffic, and the more charging stations you pass. By the time you’re in the city, EVs are just normal cars.
Screenshot
That’s pretty much how EV adoption looks in the real world, concentrated in big, wealthier metro areas while rural areas lag behind.
Here’s what I’ve run into so far:
A Tesla Model S copy, the Coil Raiden, and a Porsche Taycan copy.
Public fast chargers branded “ReVolt America,” an obvious copy of Electrify America’s stations.
A giant charging hub at the power plant with dozens of stalls and several EVs plugged in.
Chargers ICEd by gas cars parked in the EV spots.
That last one got me. Gas cars blocking chargers has been a complaint for as long as public charging has existed, and we’ve covered EV owners blocking a gas station in protest over ICEing . Rockstar recreating it tells me someone at the studio has actually tried to charge an EV in public. Probably even in Florida, which they tried to recreate here.
The EVs just work
GTA 6 is the first mainline GTA where energy matters. Gas cars burn fuel and need a pump, and EVs have a battery level and need a plug.
Rockstar could have used that to make EVs a pain. It didn’t. In my testing, the EVs have about the same range as the gas cars, charge just as fast as a fill-up, and cost the same or less to top up.
Kotaku’s range test backs that up. On the same highway loop, a Tesla Model 3 lookalike lasted 20 minutes and 23 seconds on a charge, longer than the Banshee sports car at 18 minutes and 31 seconds, and not far off an old pickup at 29 minutes and 8 seconds. Crossing the whole map by highway takes under 15 minutes, according to Kotaku.
And finding a charger isn’t a problem. Wccftech counted 120 EV chargers marked on the map, against just 57 gas stations.
From Tesla punchline to everyday car
Rockstar’s EV history starts with Coil, the series’ Tesla stand-in, named after the Tesla coil. GTA V, released in 2013, gave us the Coil Voltic, a copy of the original Lotus-based Tesla Roadster, alongside oddballs like the Cheval Surge and the Fisker Karma-inspired Khamelion.
The Voltic was quick off the line and slow everywhere else. It had the lowest top speed of any supercar in the game, which fan lore pins on its battery overheating at speed. That’s pretty much how a lot of people thought about EVs in 2013.
GTA Online added more electric cars starting in late 2017: the Rimac-inspired Coil Cyclone, then the Model S-based Coil Raiden and the Taycan-inspired Pfister Neon around the Doomsday Heist update. That same update introduced Avon Hertz, a tech billionaire whose AI tries to end the world. Rockstar never said who he was based on. Players didn’t need the help.
But those were rare, expensive toys. Nothing in GTA V needed fuel, so an EV was just a gas car without the engine noise, and you mostly saw them in the garages of players who bought them.
Electrify America is in on the joke
Electrify America noticed its in-game twin fast. The Volkswagen-owned network put out a statement on Friday saying it “will stick to charging vehicles in the real world” and adding, “We wish ReVolt America well.”
It’s a good-natured response, and probably the best free marketing the network has had in years. EA has spent most of the last decade fighting a reputation for broken chargers, even though reliability across US fast-charging networks has improved this year. Every ReVolt station I’ve used in the game worked. Not a perfect parody, then.
A little ahead of reality
GTA has always been a parody of American life. With EVs, it’s now slightly ahead of it.
Florida is one of the strongest EV markets in the country, with a 9.4% share of new passenger vehicle sales in Q2 2026 versus 7.4% nationally, according to the Southern Alliance for Clean Energy. Electrify America alone runs more than 350 chargers at over 60 Florida stations, including its biggest station yet near Orlando’s theme parks .
But real Florida still has roughly three gas stations for every public charging location, based on the Alliance for Automotive Innovation’s count of 3,267 charging locations and xMap’s count of more than 10,500 gas stations. Leonida flips that ratio.
What’s missing: home charging
There’s one piece Rockstar hasn’t nailed, at least not yet. You can’t install a charger at your place, but early in the story you’re renting. I’m not far enough in to own a property, so I don’t know whether that changes later.
It matters, because home charging is the biggest real-world advantage of an EV. Most owners leave every morning with a full battery and rarely use public chargers. If owned properties in GTA 6 come with a plug, EVs become the more convenient choice in the game, just like they are in real life for anyone with a driveway.
I also haven’t hit a mission built around EVs yet. If I find one, I’ll update this post.
Electrek’s Take
GTA works as a mirror. In 2013, the EV was a punchline: a Tesla parody that overheated if you drove it too fast. In 2026, it’s just another car in Vice City traffic, and the joke is on the guy in the pickup parked in the charging stall.
That’s a good sign of where EVs actually are. Satire goes after what’s common, and Rockstar decided EVs are common enough to be part of everyday Leonida, more so in the city than in the Keys, just like real life. And that message is reaching a huge audience. Take-Two says GTA 6 did $3.79 billion in first-day sales. Tens of millions of people are now driving EVs that charge as fast and as cheaply as gas cars, with no range anxiety. No automaker ad campaign gets close to that.
So EVs aren’t a statement in GTA anymore. They’re normal, which is exactly the point the industry has been trying to make for years.
The real Florida just needs to catch up.

810,592 Honda and Acura Vehicles Recalled Over Takata-Produced Airbag Inflators
55 photos
Photo: Honda
Toyota Motor North America recently announced that it's recalling 314,029 vehicles in the United States of America, namely older cars, sport utility vehicles, and trucks equipped with PSAN airbag inflators produced by Takata. Said campaign has an American Honda Motor counterpart now, and it's a big one.
Per the recall documentation published by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration , a whopping 810,592 vehicles from the Honda and Acura brands are being recalled stateside. The population includes models fitted with Takata airbag inflators that contain moisture-absorbing material. In a similar fashion to the Toyota recall , this one boils down to long-term propellant degradation.
The propellant can go bad when exposed to elevated temperatures, high humidity, and repeated temperature changes. In this context, degradation means the phase-stabilized ammonium nitrate propellant can burn abnormally when the airbag deploys, creating excessive pressure in the inflator housing. This, in turn, sends very sharp metal fragments through the airbag's cushion into the cabin.
"That can't happen to me," is what many would say, but do remember that iffy Takata inflators have taken the lives of more than 35 people worldwide. In the US, the NHTSA Takata Recall Spotlight cites 28 confirmed fatalities and more than 400 injuries nationwide since 2009. So yes, those inflators are really dangerous.
American Honda Motor's documentation confirms that affected inflators feature PSAN propellant and something called 13X, namely a desiccant intended to control moisture within the inflator. Despite the presence of 13X, the propellant may not perform as intended over time, fracturing more than intended. This increases the burning surface area, resulting in a higher rate of gas generation.
Photo: Honda American Honda Motor is recalling the 2012 through 2013 model year CR-V and Civic, 2013 Accord, 2013 Acura RDX, and the 2013 ILX. The recall population is restricted to vehicles that AHM dealers originally sold or customers registered in 14 states and territories with high temperatures and elevated humidity. California, Louisiana, Texas, Mississippi, and Georgia are some of them.
The rest are South Carolina, Alabama, Florida, Puerto Rico, Hawaii, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, American Samoa, and the US Virgin Islands. As you'd expect, the Civic accounts for the bulk of the recall population. Honda's compact is listed with 413,125 potentially affected cars, while the CR-V and Accord populations are estimated at 197,045 and 165,225 vehicles.
Acura contributes 20,554 examples of the RDX and 14,643 of the ILX, amounting to a grand total of 810,592 automobiles. American Honda Motor has received no reports of injuries (or worse) associated with these inflators, making this a preventive recall based on degradation analysis. The investigation stretches back to June 2020 and an analysis of desiccated PSAN inflators.
AHM found no signs of deterioration at that point, yet its statistical modeling indicated that propellant deterioration would advance far enough to create an inflator rupture risk before 2027 at the earliest. The investigation continued through November 2026, with AHM confirming that the inflators still operated within normal parameters.
Out of an abundance of caution, both the front driver- and passenger-side inflators will be replaced free of charge with new units from a different supplier, complete with a different propellant chemistry that avoids long-term degradation problems under similar conditions. Interim notification letters will be mailed on December 18, 2026. Another notification will follow once sufficient parts become available.

Would You Pay New Prius Money for This Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat?
21 photos
Photo: Instagram | phoenix_motor_collection
Everyone and their pet knows that the Dodge Challenger is no longer in production. The third generation was dropped in 2023, as that’s when the final copy rolled off the assembly line at the Brampton facility in Ontario, Canada.
However, just because one machine is no longer being put together does not make it less exciting. Most gearheads still dream about an older supercar, and some would gladly live with a proper muscle car that packs so much oomph that it can give blue-blooded exotics a run for their money. And this is definitely where the Hellcat lineup fits, because even in its most basic configuration, it offered more than enough power for exciting daily drives sprinkled with fast takeoffs.
The original Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat came out more than a decade ago as a high-performance variant of the brand’s muscle car. It had a more aggressive look on the outside, the cockpit was bedecked with some extras, and the chassis was modified. The brakes were also uprated in order to cope with the extra oomph. The model came with two separate key fobs. The black one limited the output to a more down-to-earth 500 horsepower (373 kW507 ps), whereas the red one enabled the full output capability.
This meant 707 horsepower (527 kW/717 ps), with the peak thrust being rated at 650 pound-feet (881 Nm). The 6.2-liter supercharged V8 engine, which was also introduced not only to the Challenger’s four-door sibling, the era’s Charger, but also to the Jeep Grand Cherokee Trackhawk (previous generation) and the Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat, enabled 0-60 mph (0-97 kph) in a little over 3.5 seconds. It had a 199 mph (320 kph) top speed, and could complete the 1/4-mile in 11.6 seconds at 125 mph (201 kph) on stock rubber.
Photo: Instagram | phoenix_motor_collection From here on, Dodge kept refining the Hellcat motor , launching punchier versions of its third-gen Challenger. Some of them exceeded the 800-horsepower mark, and the fastest and most powerful production muscle car to date remains the SRT Demon 170. This model ran the standing quarter mile in 8.91 seconds, with an exit speed of 151.17 mph (243.28 kph), had up to 1,025 horsepower in its top configuration, and reached 60 mph (97 kph) in a neck-snapping 1.66 seconds.
Pictured in the gallery is a 2016 model year Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat, which had 31,794 miles (51,167 km) under its belt at the time of cataloging. Thus, it’s far from being a barely-driven copy, as it has seen plenty of action over the years. However, it still looks very good, as the glossy black paint finish is on the shiny side of things. There are some red emblems on the outside, red brake calipers behind the black wheels, as well as a vented hood, and a ducktail spoiler that came from the factory.
This machine features a black leather interior and black trim. It also has white stitching for contrast, the usual SRT inserts, and there is plenty of wear on the driver’s seat. But then again, you didn’t think that it would be in top notch form, did you?
The vendor mentions stuff such as the leather upholstery, heated and ventilated front seats, heated steering wheel, and Harman Kardon audio system. The Bluetooth connectivity, Apple CarPlay, air conditioning, and navigation system are also on deck, and so are the rear parking sensors, reversing camera, and blind spot monitoring system.
Photo: Instagram | phoenix_motor_collection This Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat also has a few modifications, and the selling dealer says that it is in “mint condition.” The muscle car has reportedly never been involved in an accident, as per the clean Carfax history report mentioned in the listing. It has a clean title, and you can park it in your driveway if you really want it. By the way, the vendor also offers financing.
Speaking of the vendor, it is known as @phoenix_motor_collection on Instagram, and advertises this machine on its social media, which is where we found it. But how much does it cost to park this thing in your driveway? Well, at the time of writing, the muscle car in question had an asking price of $46,400 attached to it.
That’s basically new, range-topping Toyota Prius PHEV money, and most petrolheads and their grandmothers would tell you that you only live once, and it’s better to own a great V8-powered ride rather than a dull electrified compact. But let’s not forget that the latter comes with the factory warranty, and only the delivery miles under its belt, whereas the former has seen a lot of action over the years, and there is obviously no warranty here.
Still, if you crave a nice Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat and have less than $50,000 to blow on one, then this example could be exactly what the doctor ordered. And if you must have it, then you know what to do next, don’t you? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Phoenix Motor Collection (@phoenix_motor_collection)

Tesla officially launched in Argentina on Friday with President Javier Milei on stage in Buenos Aires, and Elon Musk joined by video from his plane to welcome the brand’s newest market. It didn’t go well.
Musk got through one line about Tesla before stalling out: “Sorry, I don’t really know what I want to say.” The call ended about two minutes in, without any real pitch for the Model 3 or Model Y that Tesla had just put on sale.
Two minutes of “I don’t know what to say”
The launch took place at Arenas Studio in Buenos Aires’ La Boca neighborhood. Milei spoke for less than eight minutes, then the host asked the room to welcome “our next guest,” and Musk popped up on the giant screen from what looked like an airplane cabin. Milei burst out laughing and bounced on his feet.
Musk started fine: “Hello, Argentina. Well, here we are. It’s a joy to share Tesla with all of you and to establish ourselves there.”

Then he started glancing off to each side. “Actually, I don’t really know what to say, other than thank you for this welcome to Tesla in Argentina,” he said. He briefly mentioned a charging network with state-owned oil company YPF, thanked the audience again, and then: “Sorry, I don’t really know what I want to say.”
And that was it. The feed cut before he even said goodbye.

A new proposed indication was not enough to get deramiocel across the regulatory finish line. The FDA has again turned away the cell therapy, which is being developed for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, for the second time in as many years.
The FDA left Capricor Therapeutics assessing its options yet again after issuing a second rejection for the biotech’s cell therapy deramiocel for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
In its complete response letter (CRL), which Capricor announced late Friday evening , the FDA said it did not consider the data provided by the biotech to establish “substantial evidence of effectiveness.” The FDA also cited “certain other clinical deficiencies,” per Capricor’s release.
Shares of the biotech crashed nearly 80% after hours on Friday to $1.63 per share, down from a closing price of $7.59 a pop.
“We are deeply disappointed for the boys and young men living with Duchenne and their families,” Capricor CEO Linda Marbán said in a prepared statement. “Deramiocel has been studied in two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, HOPE-2 and HOPE-3, both of which met their primary endpoints. We stand behind the rigor of our clinical program and the integrity of our data, and we believe the data support approval.”
Marban said the company is reviewing the CRL “carefully” and will share next steps one it has completed that evaluation.
As of Sept. 30, Capricor had cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities of around $198.5 million, according to the release. The biotech believes these funds are “sufficient to fund its planned operations for at least the next 12 months.”
This is not the first time Capricor has faced rejection for deramiocel . In its July 2025 CRL, the FDA said there was insufficient evidence to establish deramiocel’s effectiveness for cardiomyopathy associated with DMD. The agency also cited certain deficiencies regarding the therapy’s chemistry, manufacturing and controls. In a press release at the time, Capricor contended it had already addressed these concerns in previous communications and that “these materials were not reviewed by the FDA due to the timing of the CRL issuance.”
Communication between the FDA and Capricor has been contentious, to say the least. The first rejection reportedly came after an advisory committee scheduled by Nicole Verdun—then the director of the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER)'s Office of Therapeutic Products—was unilaterally canceled by then–CBER director Vinay Prasad. Verdun and her deputy Rachael Anatol were both pushed out of the agency in June last year.
Things appeared to be turning around for Capricor five months later, when the company reported positive data from the Phase 3 HOPE-3 trial , which randomized 106 patients with DMD to receive deramiocel or placebo for 12 months. Deramiocel showed statistically significant benefits in upper limb function, meeting the trial’s primary endpoint, Capricor reported in December 2025. The cell therapy also slowed decline in cardiac function as measured by left ventricular ejection fraction, satisfying the trial’s secondary endpoint.
The FDA disagreed with this assessment, however.
FDA
UPDATE: FDA disputes Capricor’s claims of Phase 3 success for DMD cell therapy
In briefing documents published Monday ahead of an advisory committee meeting for deramiocel, the FDA disagreed with Capricor’s assertion that a Phase 3 trial met its primary outcome measures.
July 27, 2026
·
3 min read
·
Heather McKenzie
Read more
In briefing documents released by the agency prior to a July 29 adcomm, the FDA wrote that HOPE-3 “did not meet its pre-specified primary and secondary efficacy endpoints, showing no statistically significant difference between deramiocel and placebo at 12 months.”
The adcomm itself also did not go Capricor’s way. The biotech had originally sought to market deramiocel for DMD cardiomyopathy, and the discussion was primarily focused on this endpoint, but these data failed to impress the FDA’s advisors, who ultimately voted 9-3 against the therapy’s approval.
Capricor then pivoted to an indication of upper limb function, which garnered a more positive discussion at the adcomm. But the change in proposed indication wasn’t enough to get deramiocel across the finish line.
Whatever path Capricor decides to take moving forward, it will do so with a smaller staff. In September, the biotech parted ways with around 10% of its workforce, a move intended “to align our organization with our near-term priorities,” CEO Linda Marbán said on a Nov. 10 call to present the company’s third quarter earnings.
The company had faith in deramiocel, significantly ramping up manufacturing at its San Diego plant to support commercial production of the therapy.
Marbán was also prepared, however, for the decision to go the other way. During the earnings call, the CEO said that if deramiocel was rejected, Capricor would assess the feedback and act “prudently based on if we think that there’s a way to establish greater efficacy and/or safety doing another clinical trial.”
The company has also initiated regulatory engagement in Europe and Japan for the cell therapy, according to its Q3 earnings release .
Deramiocel is made up of allogeneic cardiosphere-derived cells, which have been shown to exert immunomodulatory and anti-fibrotic actions, helping to preserve skeletal and cardiac muscle function in muscular dystrophies, including DMD, per Capricor .
In an opinion piece for BioSpace , biotech and Capricor consultant Elijah Stacy, who lives with DMD, described the FDA’s decision on this application as the first key test of the agency’s new “fit-for-purpose” framework , revealed in October, for regulating rare disease therapies based on patient need and realistically attainable evidence.

Last month, the FDA committed to designing a “fit-for-purpose” framework for regulating rare disease therapies based on patient need and realistically attainable evidence. With the upcoming decision for Capricor’s Duchenne muscular dystrophy cell therapy deramiocel, this paradigm faces its first key test.

John Hennessey Drives the Most Powerful Truck With a Combustion Engine, Ram 1500 TRX
12 photos
Photo: Hennessey Performance | YouTube
Hypercar builder John Hennessey got his hands on a truck with nearly hypercar performance figures. He took the all-new Ram 1500 SRT TRX, just fresh out the factory, for a spin on the track to see what it can do before he works his magic on the already monstrous contraption.
At the Pennzoil Proving Grounds at Lonestar Motorsports Park, in Sealy, Texas, he puts the all-new Ram 1500 SRT TRX through its paces. It has just arrived from the factory, and its stock days are numbered. It will get the Mammoth 1000 pack, along with some other special treats, John Hennessey reveals.
But before it undergoes transformation, John Hennessey wants to see how it compares to the previous TRX. The moment he presses the throttle, he goes, " Oh, yeah! " The transmission shifts firmly, the HEMI orchestra roars out its drama out back, and the truck seems ready to bite big chunks off the pavement.
However, even though the Ram truck looks and acts like a ferocious beast, it still makes a great and reliable daily driver. " In Texas, everybody drives a pickup truck ," says the performance guru. But not everyone drives a truck that stands out even before any aftermarket upgrade.
Photo: Hennessey Performance | YouTube He says the Ford F-150 Raptor R feels lighter, and the aluminum body has something to do with it. It is not just a feeling, but reality. A fully optioned F-150 Raptor R tips the scales at 6,090 pounds (2,762 kilograms), while the SRT TRX weighs 6,750 pounds (3,062 kilograms). That is a solid 660-pound (299-kilogram) weight gap between the two.
However, the TRX compensates with the extra power. The 6.2-liter supercharged HEMI V8 pumps out 777 horsepower (788 metric horsepower) and 680 pound-feet (922 Newton meters) of torque for a run from zero to hero (0 to 60 mph or 0 to 97 kph) in 3.5 seconds, a quarter mile in 12.2 seconds, and a top speed of 118 mph (190 kph).
In the meantime, the Raptor R has to deal with the 5.2-liter supercharged Carnivore V8, which churns out 720 horsepower (730 metric horsepower) and 640 pound-feet (868 Newton meters) of torque. That is enough to make it rocket from 0 to 60 in 3.6 seconds, run the quarter mile in 12.1 seconds, and max out at 114 mph (184 kph).
The extra weight by no means feels like a drawback. It might actually work in its favor, as John Hennessey says it feels more planted, with no compromise whatsoever on the fun factor. He congratulates Tim Kuniskis , the man who returned to Stellantis after a short-lived retirement, following former CEO Carlos Tavares’s abrupt departure, to fix the mistakes of the previous management.
Photo: Hennessey Performance | YouTube Tim Kuniskis is the man who brought back the HEMI, along with the TRX, in the Ram 1500 lineup, giving the Ford F-150 Raptor R a run for its money once again. The all-new SRT TRX is a monster from the moment it rolls off the production line.
However, Hennessey's Mammoth package is going to turn it into a drag strip and desert weapon , making it the first TRX dialed up by the Texas-based tuner after the return of the HEMI V8. And it will, indeed, rolling weapon with very reliable track capabilities, unless Hennessey Performance decides to slam it for enhanced hypercar behavior.
The upgrade brings a high-flow supercharger system, upgraded front and rear drive pulleys, a heavy-duty supercharger belt, and a crank damper pin assembly. High-flow fuel injectors, a performance air induction system, upgraded spark plugs, a revised crankcase ventilation system, a cooler thermostat, and custom engine (ECM) and transmission (TCM) calibrations will also be part of the plan.
All these mods will most likely drop the 0 to 60 time to 3.2 seconds and the quarter-mile time to just 11.4 seconds, with a trap speed of 120 mph (193 kph), because that is what the Hennessey Performance experts do for a living.
Photo: Hennessey Performance | YouTube Hennessey is keeping busy at this time of year. The tuning experts have recently delivered a VelociRaptoR to NASCAR driver Joey Logano . The truck was officially dialed up to 1,000 horsepower. The 5.2-liter supercharged V8 now makes 1,200 horsepower at the wheel.
In the meantime, Hennessey Performance is working around the clock to fine-tune the Blackbird, its all-new in-house-developed supercar and the first since the Venom F5. While the most powerful Venom came with 2,031 horsepower and a manual transmission, the Blackbird is more tamed in a fun way.
Hennessey’s upcoming model is an aerospace-inspired (no, it won’t fly and it won’t flip mid-air like the Tesla Roadster) hypercar with zero screens and analog everything. It is powered by an Ilmor-developed 6.2-liter naturally aspirated V8 that revs past 9,000 rpm and puts out 850 horsepower.
The Blackbird is Hennessey’s only second model built from the ground up after the Venom F5, unveiled back in 2020. The Venom GT doesn't count.

Moparhead Went To Buy a '57 Chrysler New Yorker, Drove Home in a Super-Rare 1963 Chrysler 300J
56 photos
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile
Back in the early sixties, Ma’ Mopar had a problem: the cars weren’t the best-looking ones in Motor City, but its engines were gunning for apex predator crowns all over the place. That conundrum put buyers under a lot of second-though indecision, and nothing illustrates that hesitation more than the elusive Chrysler 300J from 1963. Sources note that around 100 are known today, which is an overwhelming 25% of all original production. One of those incredible relics just made a guest star appearance at MCACN 2026.
Nothing tests a car guy’s poker face quite like showing up to buy one classic Mopar and watching the seller suddenly develop cold feet. Back in 2025, Omaha enthusiast Kurt Brueske drove out to inspect an all-original, 40,000-mile 1957 Chrysler New Yorker coupe finished in Ruby Red with a black roof. His buddy chickened out at the eleventh hour, then casually offered his 1963 Chrysler 300J instead. Brueske barely blinked.
That glorious consolation prize recently stole the spotlight at the Muscle Car and Corvette Nationals, the grand assembly of classic Americana royalty in Rosemont, Illinois. That’s a stone’s throw away from Chicago, which is where Lou Costabile hangs around when he’s not shooting classics at point blank. With his camera!
The 300J is a car of many special traits, but the fender tag is not one of those. It doesn’t have one. Look all you like, take the sonar and the magnifying glass underhood and the greatest team of detectives, and you still won’t be able to locate a fender tag. Mostly because it’s not on the fenders, hence it can’t be a fender tag. But more importantly, because it’s not in the engine bay.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile Chrysler tucked the 1963 trim tag down by the driver-side door hinge. It confirms body code 842 for the coupe, paint code WW1 for Oyster White, and rich Claret metallic-red leather. Wearing Nebraska plate 80-121, the hardtop fits Brueske’s Omaha club pedigree beside his 1962 300H. Even those rocket-nozzle taillights are pure "unobtainium," miraculous new-old-stock spares a previous owner somehow unearthed (probably from the end of the rainbow).
Climb inside and the 1963 cabin feels like a mid-century lounge with an attitude problem. You grip a squared steering wheel shaped like a vintage television screen (alright, anyone 40 and younger, go look it up), facing pushbutton TorqueFlite keys, a 150-mph speedometer, a console tachometer, and a low air-conditioning vent cryptically nicknamed a "crotch cooler," because of its direct line of sight to the target.
Locking the door requires pushing the interior handle forward – I so wish they made cool features like this standard again! – and don’t even bother to read the tach while driving at night. Why did carmakers choose to put the rev gauge on the center console, and make it about the size of a wristwatch is anyone’s guess.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile I’m putting my money on the fact that people were sharper in more ways than today, and could actually use a rotary-dial perpetual calendar without asking a computer for directions. All that executive eccentricity made total sense for Chrysler’s legendary Letter Series, born in 1955 when the C-300 welded NASCAR thunder onto country-club luxury.
Across eleven consecutive model years from 1955 through 1965, Chrysler marched alphabetically from C-300 to 300L, cranking out just 16,857 letter cars, a microscopic 1.29% of total brand output. In 1970, the 300 Hurst revival briefly crashed the party with 503 more brutes, sealing the bloodline’s cult aura. No, I don’t think the 300M from this millennium is a worthy heir to the Letter Series throne.
When the ninth installment arrived for 1963, Highland Park quietly skipped the letter "I" because Detroit figured shoppers might confuse it with the numeral 1. Thus, the 300J was born, wearing crisp, finless sheetmetal representing Virgil Exner’s final bow before former Ford stylist Elwood Engel took over in 1962. Study the scalloped C-pillar and recessed, Thunderbird-like taillights, though, and you can already spot Engel’s sharp fingerprints creeping into the metal.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile Unfortunately for Chrysler’s bean counters, buyers stayed away in droves, turning the 1963 Chrysler 300J into the scarcest Letter Series car ever cobbled together. Between October 22, 1962, and June 18, 1963, assembly stalled at exactly 400 cars. Every single one of those 400 units rolled out as a two-door hardtop coupe. Drop-top fans defected to the cheaper, non-letter 300 Sport Series, which even paced the 1963 Indy 500.
Slice those 400 coupes by drivetrain and the rarity gets downright absurd. Exactly 393 buyers stuck with the standard pushbutton three-speed TorqueFlite automatic paired to a 3.23:1 rear axle, leaving a microscopic seven daredevils who checked the no-cost box for the heavy-duty, floor-shifted 3-speed manual and its 3.91:1 Sure-Grip differential.
Under the hood, nobody hesitated: all 400 units of the “Three Hundred J” (that’s what the emblems say) roared out of Detroit packing the exclusive 390-horsepower, 413-cubic-inch short-ram V8.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile One glance at the window sticker explains why showrooms stayed quiet. A brand-new 1963 300J demanded a stiff $5,200 base price, towering over the $3,400 base 300 Sport parked nearby. Because the 390-horsepower 413 Wedge came baked into the ticket, Chrysler listed no regular optional engine or upgrade price, though competition-spec 426-cubic-inch Maximum Performance Wedge monsters existed via unpriced special order for dedicated racers.
Still, anybody grumbling about the tab stopped complaining once that broad hood popped open. Chrysler’s cast-iron, overhead-valve 413-cubic-inch (6.8-liter) wedge V8 featured a 9.6:1 compression, solid lifters, a 268-degree camshaft, and high-flow cast-iron headers. Crowned by aluminum 15-inch cross-ram manifolds feeding twin Carter AFB four-barrel carburetors, it churned out 390 horsepower at 4,800 rpm and a rib-cracking 485 lb-ft of torque at 3,600 rpm (395 PS, 658 Nm).
Dyno engineers had learned a clever trick since the 30-inch long-ram intakes of 1960 and 1961: opening internal plenum passages to 15 inches shifted that ram-charging torque wallop from roughly 2,200 rpm up near 3,000 rpm. As Brueske gleefully noted, this tailored heavyweight matched an A12 Road Runner’s factory 390-horsepower punch. Shoving 4,000 pounds along a 122-inch wheelbase, an automatic 300J blasted from 0 to 60 mph in 8.0 seconds flat.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile Keep your right loafer buried and the big Chrysler stormed through the quarter-mile in 15.4 to 15.8 seconds at up to 96 mph before topping out at a hair-raising 142 mph. Naturally, accountants panicked after 1963. For the 1964 300K, Chrysler slashed the price, demoted the short-ram V8 to an option, ditched standard leather, and swapped the 150-mph speedometer for a tame 120-mph dial, boosting volume to 3,647 cars.
That sensible corporate retreat accidentally crowned the 1963 300J as the final, unfiltered "banker's hot rod," all silk suit on the outside and freight-train menace underneath. When Brueske finally pointed this amazing power cruiser toward Nebraska in 2025, he felt every ounce of that effortless cross-ram shove firsthand. Sure, he missed out on his buddy’s 1957 New Yorker, yet stumbling backward into a 1-of-400 Mopar icon might be the luckiest detour ever.
